title: WQL Markdown Query Blocks & Dashboard Pipeline Model
subtitle: A consistent mental model for piping WQL lists into graphs, binding reusable values for calculations, and providing stage-aware typeahead inside ```query blocks

components.eyebrow: Unified WQL Mental Model · ```query Blocks & Dashboards
components.title: Select a List. Pipe to a Reducer. Pipe to a Graph. Bind Named Values.
components.body: Today, WQL feels split across four disconnected dialects: legacy aggregators (sum:tis{}), content finders (:journal{}), multi-line query documents, and fence-suffix dashboard overrides (```query:bar-2). The unified model collapses every ```query block into one left-to-right pipeline: Source List | Function Reducer | Chart Sink, with let-style named bindings (name = ...) that can be reused across calculations and typeahead that adapts to the active stage.

components.title: Mental Model Simplification Goals
components.body: Replacing fragmented syntax rules with a single composable grammar inside standard Markdown ```query fences.

items.label: Pipeline Anatomy
items.detail: 1. List Source  2. Value Reducer  3. Graph Sink

items.label: Reusable Bindings
items.detail: Named values feed downstream math & multi-series charts

components.title: 1. Why Today's Model Feels Inconsistent
components.body: Authors currently have to switch mental models depending on whether they are filtering notes, charting a single metric, combining two series in a calculation, or laying out a dashboard card.

components.title: Current Fragmentation vs. Unified Pipeline Mental Model
components.body: How the current inconsistencies are resolved into one predictable rule set.
rows: Filter a list of workouts or segments
:journal{effort:snatch} or :segment{effort:snatch}
Returns a list, but it is unclear how this list turns into a chart without switching to sum:metric{} syntax.
Every query starts as a List Source (:journal, :segment, :session, @today). Unpiped, it renders as a list or table.
Graph a metric from that list
sum:tis{effort:snatch} by {week} inside ```query:timeseries
Chart choice lives on the Markdown fence (```query:timeseries) while data lives inside, or mixes legacy sum:metric with colon heads.
Pipe the list into a reducer and a chart sink inside a plain ```query block: :segment{effort:snatch} | :sum{metric:tis} by {week} | :timeseries{}
Reuse values in another calculation
Undocumented document mode: work = :sum{metric:tis}, ratio = work / recovery, show ratio
Feels like a separate mini-language; unclear whether variables hold lists, time series, or scalars, and how they reach a chart.
First-class Named Bindings: any line can bind name = <pipeline or formula>, and the final pipe or show stage sends those named values straight to a graph.
Configure chart goals, spans, and layout
Fence tag suffixes: ```query:goal-rings-2 goal=$hangGoal
Splits parameters between fence info-string attributes and query body; breaks standard Markdown code-fence expectations.
Keep fence as ```query (optional layout span). Chart parameters live inside the chart sink braces: | :goal-rings{goal:$hangGoal, span:2}.

components.title: Core Design Principle: Everything Starts as a List, Everything Renders at the Tail
components.body: You never have to ask 'Am I writing a content query, an analytics query, or a dashboard widget?' You always start with a list of domain records, optionally pipe (|) it through reducers or formulas to produce numeric series/scalars, and pipe (|) the result into a dashboard visualization.

components.title: 2. The 3-Stage Pipeline Mental Model
components.body: Inside any ```query block, data flows left-to-right through three predictable stages separated by the pipe operator (|). Omitting later stages simply stops the pipeline earlier with a sensible default view.

components.title: Anatomy of a WQL Pipeline
components.body: Each stage has a single job, a distinct prefix sigil, and a clear input/output contract.

items.title: :source{filters} or @dataset
items.body: Selects a list of items from the vault or active page context. Examples: :journal{equipment:barbell}, :segment{effort:snatch} last 8w, :session{}, @today, @session. If the pipeline stops here, the block renders an interactive List or Rows Table.

items.title: | :reducer{metric} by {dim}
items.body: Consumes the list from Stage 1 and projects/reduces numeric metrics across buckets. Examples: | :sum{metric:totalVolume} by {week}, | :max{metric:resistance}, | :count{}. Chained reducers (:sum by {session} | :avg{}) reduce the previous stage in memory.

items.title: | :chart{presentation}
items.body: Consumes the reduced series or list and chooses the dashboard element. Examples: | :timeseries{}, | :bar{stack:effort}, | :value{unit:kg}, | :goal-rings{goal:10000}. If omitted on a numeric pipeline, the block infers :value (1 point), :bar (categories), or :timeseries (time buckets).

components.title: Progressive Disclosure: From Simple Filter to Dashboard Graph
components.body: A user learns one syntax and progressively adds pipes as their question becomes more analytical.

items.title: :journal{effort:thruster, intent:benchmark} last 12w
items.body: Selects all benchmark journal notes containing thrusters in the last 12 weeks. No reducer or chart stage is present, so the ```query block renders a clickable Note Card List.

items.meta: Step 2 · Pipe List to Count / Table
items.title: :journal{effort:thruster} last 12w | :count{} by {format} | :bar{}
items.body: Takes that exact same list of journal notes, counts how many occurred per workout format (for-time, emom, amrap), and pipes the grouped counts into a horizontal Bar Chart.

items.meta: Step 3 · Pipe Segment List to Volume Timeseries
items.title: :segment{effort:thruster} last 12w | :sum{metric:totalVolume} by {week} | :timeseries{}
items.body: Selects executed thruster segments over 12 weeks, sums their tonnage per Monday-aligned civil week, and plots the weekly progression as a Timeseries line/area chart.

items.meta: Step 4 · Multi-Stage Reduction to Hero Stat
items.title: :segment{effort:thruster} last 12w | :sum{metric:totalVolume} by {session} | :max{} | :value{label:"Peak Session Volume"}
items.body: Sums thruster volume per session first, then finds the maximum single-session volume across the 12-week window, and renders it as a single Hero Value card.

components.title: 3. Piping WQL Lists into Graphs in Different Ways
components.body: The same underlying WQL list can drive completely different dashboard visuals depending on how Stage 2 buckets the list and which Stage 3 graph sink receives the pipe.

components.title: Dashboard Graph Sinks & How Lists Pipe Into Them
components.body: Every dashboard element accepts a predictable data shape from the preceding pipe stage.
columns: How the List Is Piped (Markdown WQL)
rows: :list{} / :table{}
Unreduced item list (:note, :journal, :segment, :session)
:segment{effort:snatch} last 4w | select date, resistance in kg, reps | order by resistance desc | limit 5 | :table{}
Sortable, paginated tabular record view or rich linked note list.
:value{}
Single scalar (1 series × 1 point)
@today | :sum{metric:tis} | :value{label:"Today TIS", goal:450}
KPI Hero Stat Card with unit, optional delta badge, and target comparison.
:bar{} / :stacked-bar{}
Categorical series (grouped by tag, effort, discipline, or day)
:segment{} last 4w | :sum{metric:totalVolume} by {discipline, week} | :stacked-bar{}
Grouped or stacked bar chart comparing volume across movement disciplines.
:timeseries{}
Time-bucketed series (by {day}, by {week}, or .rollup(2w))
:segment{effort:back-squat} last 12w | :max{metric:calc.e1rm} by {week} | :timeseries{smooth:true}
Multi-line or area time-series progression chart with civil-date tooltips.
:donut{} / :zone-distribution{}
Part-to-whole categorical breakdown (by {intensity} or {domain})
@session | :sum{metric:elapsed} by {intensity} | :donut{}
Proportional ring/donut or intensity-zone distribution bar with percentage legend.
:toplist{}
Ranked categorical reduction
:segment{} last 8w | :count{} by {effort} | :toplist{limit:5}
Ranked leaderboard bars showing top movements or benchmarks by frequency or load.
:goal-rings{}
1–3 scalar or ratio values paired with targets
@today | :sum{metric:totalVolume} | :goal-rings{goal:$dailyVolumeGoal}
Concentric activity rings showing completion percentage against fixed or calculated targets.

components.title: 4. Defining Named Values for Reuse in Calculations & Graphs
components.body: A ```query block stays simple for one-liners, but scales naturally when you name intermediate pipelines. Any line of the form name = <pipeline or formula> defines a reusable value (either a time-aligned series or a scalar) that downstream lines can reference by name or $name.

components.title: 3 Rules for Named Values Inside ```query Blocks
components.body: How bindings work without turning WQL into a complicated programming language.

items.title: defaults sets the block's frame
items.body: An optional top line (defaults by {week} last 12w) sets the default time window and grouping bucket for every query line in the block, eliminating repetitive suffixes.

items.title: name = pipeline or expression
items.body: Assigning a pipeline (acute = :segment{} last 1w | :avg{metric:sessionLoad}) binds a value. Formulas (acwr = acute / chronic) combine named values using +, -, *, /, or corr(a, b), automatically aligning buckets when grouped or dividing scalars when ungrouped.

items.badge: Rule 3 · Pipe Bindings to a Graph
items.title: show a, b | :chart{}
items.body: The final line selects which defined values to plot and pipes them into a chart sink: show acute, chronic | :timeseries{} or show acwr | :value{goal:1.2}. If there is only one formula at the end, it renders automatically.

components.title: Concrete Markdown Examples: Named Values in Calculations
components.body: How authors write multi-step calculations and pipe them to graphs inside a ```query block.
rows: 1. Workload Ratio (Scalar Calculation → Gauge/Value)
acute and chronic evaluate to 7-day and 28-day scalar averages. acwr divides them. The final pipe sends acwr into a Value card with target 1.0.
2. Multi-Series Overlay + Derived Ratio (Series Math → Timeseries)
push and pull share the 12-week weekly buckets. balance computes the weekly pull-to-push percentage pointwise. The block can plot push vs. pull bars or the balance trend.
3. Relative Intensity (% of 1RM using a Named Scalar Baseline)
best_squat is a scalar 52-week PR. weekly_top is an 8-week series. Dividing a series by a scalar broadcasts best_squat across every week to plot %1RM.
4. Page-Level Shared Variables ($token & @dataset)

--- (Frontmatter)
dashboard.target_tis: 1200
dashboard.lift: snatch
---
work = :segment{effort:$lift} last 4w | :sum{metric:tis}
remaining = $target_tis - work
show work | :goal-rings{goal:$target_tis}
Frontmatter dashboard.* keys expose interactive header controls ($lift, $target_tis) that substitute into any block's pipelines, formulas, and chart goals.

components.title: Keep Scope Simple: Block-Local Names + Frontmatter Page Tokens
components.body: To keep the mental model effortless: plain identifiers (acute, best_squat) are local to the ```query block where they are defined so blocks can be reordered or copied freely. Values that need to be shared across multiple blocks on a dashboard page are declared once in frontmatter (or a page-level ```query:defs block) and referenced with the $name sigil.

components.title: 3b. Bridging Note Lists → Event Math & Focused $note ($thisnote) Context
components.body: When Stage 1 selects a list of Notes (:journal{}, :note{}) and Stage 2 pipes into a numeric reducer (| :sum{}), QueryService.sourceEventsFromFind automatically resolves the EventRecord stream owned by those notes (via store.getEventsForNote(note.id)) and aggregates them in memory. To focus on a specific note or break down metrics by equipment, WQL exposes built-in host context tokens ($note / @note) alongside two architectural gaps that must be closed.

components.title: Structural Audit: What Works Today vs. What Needs to Close
components.body: Evaluating how well the current engine handles Note-to-Event math, $thisnote scoping, and by {equipment} grouping.

items.title: Note List | Reducer Bridge & $note Token
items.body: Piping :journal{...} | :sum{metric:reps} already resolves all EventRecords belonging to the matched notes and aggregates them. Furthermore, entityScope.ts already binds $note (the active note ID) and $scope (note:<id>), and accepts {note:$note} on :note, :session, :segment, and reducers.

items.title: by {equipment} on Event Reducers
items.body: In QueryService.ts, loadNoteTags() only loads note_tags when touching untyped 'tags', and factTagValue() does not resolve typed note tags (equipment, domain, format) or effort-level equipment. Grouping | :sum{metric:reps} by {equipment} returns 'unassigned' unless event facts inherit Effort/Note equipment metadata.

items.title: Focusing Events After a Note Source
items.body: Today, a reducer stage (:sum{metric:reps, effort:thruster}) filters facts simultaneously while aggregating. Adding an explicit | :segment{...} expansion stage (or @note dataset alias for $thisnote) lets authors filter the note's child events once and reuse that focused event list across multiple named calculations.

components.title: Markdown Scenarios: Note Lists, $thisnote ($note) Context, and Reps by Equipment
components.body: Concrete ```query blocks showing how authors write Note-to-Event calculations and single-note equipment breakdowns.
rows: A. Current Note Context ($note / @note) → Reps by Equipment

1. $note (or $thisnote / @note) resolves to the current Note UUID.
2. Fetches all execution EventRecords belonging to this note.
3. Sums reps grouped by each movement's equipment (kettlebell, barbell, pullup-bar) and pipes to a Bar or Donut chart.
B. List of Notes → Narrow to Specific Events → Math

1. bench_notes selects the list of benchmark journal notes once.
2. kb_reps and bb_reps pipe that note list's child events into weekly rep sums focused by equipment.
3. Plots weekly kettlebell vs. barbell reps as a stacked bar chart.
C. This Note vs. Historical Note List Baseline
Compares the equipment rep breakdown of the current note ($note) directly against the 8-week average of all 'for-time' journal notes, aligning buckets by {equipment}.
D. Focusing on High-Intensity Events Inside a Note
Binds note_events to only the high-intensity segment events of the current note, then derives both total reps and peak load by equipment from that focused event stream.

components.title: 5. Markdown Dashboard Composition Contract
components.body: A dashboard is just a Markdown note. Prose headings and questions above a ```query block become the card's title and subtitle; the pipeline inside the block defines the data and the graph.

components.title: How Markdown Elements Map to Dashboard Cards
components.body: Zero hidden JSON state: every visual element on the dashboard corresponds 1:1 to readable Markdown.

items.title: Global Controls & Tokens
items.body: dashboard: true enables the grid view. dashboard.window: [8w, 12w, 52w] and dashboard.lift: [snatch, clean] render interactive segmented filter pills at the top of the page and bind $window and $lift.

items.title: Card Title & Coaching Question
items.body: A ### Heading directly above a ```query fence becomes the widget card title. An optional paragraph between the heading and fence becomes the muted coaching question subtitle.

items.title: ```query [span]
items.body: The fence tag stays clean: ```query (or ```query span=2 / span=full for grid width). The visualization type is owned by the pipeline's terminal | :chart{} stage so the query is self-describing.

items.title: Bindings + Pipeline
items.body: Contains defaults, named value assignments (x = ...), and the output pipeline (| :bar{}). Clicking the card in View mode opens the contextual WQL composer; editing in Markdown mode provides live typeahead.

components.title: 6. Context-Aware Typeahead Inside ```query Blocks
components.body: Writing WQL in Markdown feels effortless when the editor knows which stage of the pipeline the cursor is in and suggests only valid heads, metrics, tags, and user-defined variable names.

components.title: The 6 Typeahead Slots Inside a ```query Fence
components.body: How the autocomplete engine adapts as the author types left-to-right and top-to-bottom.
rows: Start of line, or after =
1. Source / Dataset / Variable Slot

• Source heads (:journal, :segment, :session, :note, :effort)
• Page datasets (@today, @session)
• In-block named values (acute, best_squat) for formula authoring
• Block keywords (defaults, show)
Accepting a colon head inserts :segment{ and immediately opens the Filter Key menu inside the braces.
Inside {...} before :
2. Stage-Scoped Filter / Param Key Slot

• On :journal/:note → domain:, format:, equipment:, intent:, effort:, tags:, text:
• On :segment → effort:, discipline:, intensity:, grade:
• On :sum/:avg → metric:, plus fact dimensions
• On :bar/:goal-rings → goal:, unit:, label:, limit:, stack:
• Excludes keys already used in the same {...} block
Accepting a key inserts effort: and immediately opens the Filter Value menu for that key.
Inside {...} after key:
3. Dynamic Vault Value Slot

• effort: → EffortResolver slugs + aliases (thruster, back-squat)
• equipment:/domain:/format: → live indexed TagStore values
• metric: → base metrics (tis, totalVolume), calc.* targets, and <effort>.<metric>
• goal:/value → $frontmatterTokens and scalar named bindings
Inserts value (quoting if needed); typing | inside braces re-triggers value completions for OR alternatives.
After closing } of a Source or Reducer
4. Stage Suffix & Pipe Slot

• by {} (opens valid grouping dimensions for current target)
• last (offers 7d, 4w, 8w, 12w)
• from (offers YYYY-MM-DD range snippet)
• .rollup() (on reducers)
• | (advance to next pipeline stage)
• Hides singleton suffixes already present on the stage
Accepting by {} places cursor inside braces and lists target-valid dimensions (day, week, effort, discipline).
After | (top-level pipe)
5. Downstream Pipeline Stage Slot

• If after a List Source: Reducers (:sum, :avg, :max, :min, :count, :last, :delta), Row pipes (select, order by, limit), or List Sinks (:table, :list)
• If after a Reducer / Formula: Chained Reducers or Graph Sinks (:timeseries, :bar, :stacked-bar, :value, :donut, :toplist, :goal-rings)
• Never suggests Sources (:journal) after a pipe
If the previous stage already bound a metric, accepting :max{} needs no metric: key; accepting a chart sink places cursor in {params}.
In a formula line or after show / $
6. Named Value & Token Reference Slot

• Typing after show or in an arithmetic expression suggests all locally bound names (acute, chronic, push, pull) with their inferred shape badge (Scalar vs. Weekly Series) and unit
• Typing $ anywhere suggests frontmatter dashboard.* tokens ($lift, $target_tis) with their current active default value
Warns inline if a formula combines incompatible dimensions without a default bucket or references an undefined name.

components.title: Typeahead Visual & Interaction Details in the Block
components.body: Making completions self-teaching so users do not need to memorize WQL reference docs.

items.title: Show Data Shape in the Popup
items.body: Every completion row shows what it produces or expects: :segment{...} shows [List · Events], :sum{...} shows [Reducer → Series/Scalar], :timeseries{} shows [Graph · Time Series], and local variables like best_squat show [Local Scalar · 140 kg].

items.title: Inline Stage Preview Strip
items.body: While the cursor is inside a ```query block, a compact status footer at the bottom of the fence shows the live evaluation of the current line (e.g., 'Stage 1: 42 segments → Stage 2: 12 weekly buckets → Stage 3: :timeseries') or highlights any missing binding.

items.title: Fence Text ↔ Visual Composer
items.body: Because ```query blocks use a canonical pipeline grammar, clicking 'Edit' on a rendered chart card can open the visual pill composer, and any change writes back clean, human-readable pipeline text into the Markdown fence.

components.title: 7. End-to-End Authoring Walkthrough
components.body: Tracing how a user writes a ```query block from scratch with typeahead, pipes a list into a calculation, and renders a dashboard graph.

items.title: Type ```query in Markdown
items.body: Typing ```q suggests ```query. Pressing Enter inserts the fenced block and immediately opens Slot 1 completions (Sources, Datasets, defaults, or variable binding).

items.title: Type defaults by {week} last 8w
items.body: Selecting defaults offers by {} and last. Inside by {}, typeahead lists calendar and tag dimensions (week, day, effort, discipline). Every line below now inherits weekly bucketing over 8 weeks.

items.meta: 3 · Filter List & Pipe to Named Value
items.title: Type snatch_vol = :segment{effort:snatch} | :sum{metric:totalVolume}
items.body: After =, user picks :segment{ (List Source), picks effort:snatch from live EffortResolver completions, types |, and picks :sum{metric:totalVolume}. The editor registers snatch_vol as a [Weekly Series · kg].

items.title: Type clean_vol = :segment{effort:clean-and-jerk} | :sum{metric:totalVolume} and ratio = (snatch_vol / clean_vol) * 100
items.body: As the user types ratio = (, typeahead immediately offers snatch_vol and clean_vol at the top of the list because they are in-scope numeric bindings defined above.

items.title: Type show snatch_vol, clean_vol | :stacked-bar{unit:kg}
items.body: After show, typeahead offers snatch_vol, clean_vol, and ratio. After |, typeahead knows the input is 2 weekly series and ranks :timeseries{}, :bar{}, and :stacked-bar{} first. Moving the cursor outside the fence renders the live Stacked Bar Chart.

components.title: Backward Compatibility & Clean Migration Path
components.body: Existing single-line aggregate queries (sum:tis{} by {week}) and fence suffixes (```query:timeseries) continue to parse and run via the normalizer, but all typeahead, documentation, and composer write-backs emit the unified colon-pipeline syntax (:segment{} | :sum{metric:tis} by {week} | :timeseries{}) so the mental model converges on one consistent pattern.

components.title: 8. Architecture Deepening, Browser Memory & Targeted Ticket Plan
components.body: Delivering the unified pipeline syntax, Note-to-Event math, $thisnote scoping, by {equipment} grouping, and stage-aware typeahead across 6 sequential, independently testable tickets optimized for browser memory and sub-10ms warm query execution.

components.title: Browser Speed & Memory-Efficiency Invariants
components.body: Architectural constraints ensuring multi-widget dashboards and multi-stage Query Documents run with minimal heap allocation and zero redundant IndexedDB roundtrips.

items.title: Fetch Once per Named List
items.body: When a Query Document binds bench = :journal{...} and pipes it into 3 reducers (kb = bench | :sum{...}), the runner resolves matching Note IDs and EventRecords once and shares the readonly EventRecord[] slice across all downstream branches.

items.title: Zero Full-Store Fact Cloning
items.body: Instead of EventRecord[].flatMap(projectEventToFacts) allocating intermediate AnalyticsDataPoint objects for every metric in the store, filter by metricKey and time window during iteration and resolve Effort/Note dimensions via O(1) interned Map lookups.

items.title: Wire queryCache.ts + Batch Bundles
items.body: Wire coalescingEventStore() so 8 dashboard widgets sharing an 8w window join 1 in-flight IndexedDB range read, and batch NoteRelationBundle lookups once per distinct noteId.

items.title: Drop Raw Fact Arrays After Reduction
items.body: Cap QueryCache at 64 entries (invalidated by BroadcastChannel 'wodwiki.analytics') and omit the raw matched: AnalyticsDataPoint[] array from cached widget results unless explicit drill-down inspection is requested.

components.title: Targeted Implementation Tickets & Testable Acceptance Gates
